docs.purpose: The operator's front page: a grid of ten tiles, each a doorway to one internal tool - data quality, market metrics, lead-feed testing, the parcel cost model, the flight centre watchlist, the configuration control panel, app health, user management, notifications, and security. It is navigation only; it loads no data of its own and shows no numbers.
docs.data_story: This surface reaches **no API contract at all** — every value it shows is local, passed in as a prop, or read from the device.
docs.under_126: **RE-PROJECT** — it writes nothing and holds no Layer-3 store, so the move is short — the server already assembles the payload and only the rendering is client-side. It renders through the STATIC renderer (content source and SEO, or a declared redirect alone), reading no contract. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

versioning.why: It renders no payload at all, so there is nothing for a consumer to depend on and no compatibility promise to make.

inputs.why: It takes no input: a hand-written grid of ten links with no fetch, no hook and no props.

outputs.why: Forced on STATIC, and true here: the file contains no mutation, no form and no action.

state.why: No hook, no store, no useState — one unconditional render.

staleness.why: The tile list is source code; it changes only when the file is deployed.

session.why: classifyRoute reaches the admin arm on the first disjunct — pathname === "/admin" — before any authenticated or public prefix is tried.

rls_class.why: It reaches no table, so no policy class applies.

checks.why: Every tile must point at a route that exists — the retired nested flight-center link was already repointed once, and a dangling tile is how an operator finds a 308 instead of a tool.
Each tile is a link whose accessible name is its visible heading; there are no explicit aria-labels, so the name depends entirely on the copy staying meaningful.

errors.why: Nothing can fail: no fetch, no boundary, no error.tsx sibling.

emits.why: No captureEvent, no track, no ledger — a tile click is invisible to telemetry.

offers.why: An internal operator tool renders no sponsored placement; no offers/placements table is reached from any file it owns.

metering.why: Nothing here is billable or quota-bearing: no usage_events / ledger write is reached from this surface or its contracts.

config.why: No tunable of any kind is read; the tile list is a literal.

limitations.what: The spec and the code describe different surfaces
limitations.measured: Spec 26 §3.1 names /admin the Pipeline Dashboard and lists this file as its target, but the live page is a pure link hub with no pipeline panel.

limitations.what: Three of the fifteen admin routes have no tile
limitations.measured: /admin/lead-feed/inspector and /admin/pipeline/step-output are reachable only by link from another page, and /admin/lead-feed/flight-center is a retired redirect.

notes: Spec 26 Sec 3.1 names '/admin' the Pipeline Dashboard and its Target Files list src/app/admin/page.tsx, but the live page is a pure link hub with no pipeline panel - the spec and the code describe different surfaces. Spec 26 Sec 5 also records Spec 76 as sharing this file. Ten tiles vs the 15 admin routes measured here: /admin/lead-feed/inspector and /admin/pipeline/step-output are reached only from other pages, and /admin/lead-feed/flight-center is a retired redirect. identity.owner is UNRESEARCHED estate-wide: no owner registry exists in the tree, so naming one would be an invention rather than a measurement. a11y.touch_target_min_px is UNRESEARCHED because its vocabulary (UNRESEARCHED or an integer >= 44) has no member for a desktop-only admin page that declares no floor.

measured_gate.why: classifyRoute('/admin') reaches the admin-pages arm `pathname === '/admin' || pathname.startsWith('/admin/')` - the first disjunct matches exactly - and returns 'admin'. It is checked before every authenticated/public-prefix arm.

programme.why: An admin surface that operates the PLATFORM (users, entitlements, security, tunables, pipeline health) rather than either product specifically.
